title: PESTLE Analysis
subtitle: You're entering a new market, geography, or sector and you need to understand the
useWhen: external forces that could accelerate or kill your plan political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental.
howToUse: Developed by Francis Aguilar at Harvard in 1967, PESTLE is a macro-environment scan across six dimensions: Political (government policy and stability), Economic (growth, inflation, interest rates), Social (demographics, culture, behaviour trends), Technological (innovation, disruption, digital adoption), Legal (regulations, compliance), Environmental (sustainability, climate, physical). AI has broad knowledge across all six dimensions and can generate a detailed PESTLE in minutes when given the right context.
steps: Define the market, geography, and industry before prompting context is everything.
Ask AI to flag which PESTLE factors are currently most active or fast-changing.
Turn the highest-impact factors into assumptions in your Lean Canvas.

Revisit PESTLE before any major market entry or strategic shift. Read the macro environment before it reads you Before Monzo launched in the UK, its team ran a PESTLE analysis and identified two critical factors: FCA regulatory changes opening challenger bank licensing, and a generational shift in how under-35s trusted traditional banks. Neither was in the existing competitor analysis. Those two factors not the product features became the foundation of Monzo's go-to-market timing and positioning. IN PRACTICE
origin: Francis Aguilar, Harvard Business School — Scanning the Business Environment, 1967
promptBody:
Act as a macro-environment analyst using the PESTLE framework.
Business context        :  [YOUR INDUSTRY AND WHAT YOU DO]
Market / geography  :  [SPECIFIC MARKET YOU ARE ANALYSING]
Decision                       :  [WHAT YOU ARE DECIDING BASED ON THIS ANALYSIS]
Analyse all six PESTLE dimensions:
POLITICAL                  :  Government, policy, trade, stability
ECONOMIC                :  Growth, inflation, consumer spending, rates
SOCIAL                        :  Demographics, culture, behaviour trends
TECHNOLOGICAL     :  Innovation, AI, digital adoption, disruption
LEGAL: Regulations, compliance, IP, data law
ENVIRONMENTA L  :  Sustainability, ESG, climate impact
For each: give 2–3 specific factors and their likely impact on my business.
Flag the top 2 highest-risk factors I should act on now.

proTip:
Run PESTLE before entering any new geography  especially India, Southeast Asia, or the
Middle East where political and legal environments change faster than most founders
expect. The factors that kill international expansion are almost always in the P and L
dimensions, not the market size.
